title: CVE-2026-76418: Cisco Secure Firewall Zero-Day Exploited in SSL VPN Attacks
content_md: Cisco has released security updates for CVE-2026-76418, a high-severity zero-day vulnerability affecting the Remote Access SSL VPN service in Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) software. The flaw is being actively exploited in the wild and can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to force a vulnerable firewall to reload, causing a denial-of-service (DoS) condition and disrupting remote access. Cisco assigned the vulnerability a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.6. The flaw requires no authentication or user interaction and has low attack complexity. Its primary security consequence is loss of availability rather than confidentiality or integrity compromise. Cisco has not associated the vulnerability with remote code execution or confirmed data theft. The vulnerability is particularly important because edge security devices and VPN gateways are often directly exposed to the internet and provide critical access to corporate environments. Repeated exploitation could force affected appliances to restart and interrupt VPN connectivity for remote employees and administrators. Cisco disclosed the vulnerability on October 28, 2026, after its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) became aware of active exploitation during October.
